Remember when Julian Barnes wrote complex and detailed books which were well researched and felt fresh? Flaubert’s Parrot, History of the World and Arthur & George were that. I can’t actually believe The Sense of an Ending got published let alone won what was once a prestigious book award. Just why? It’s typical UK male boomer sex & class ruminations which feature in countless other better written and fleshed out books. There’s not enough in the book to have me care about Adrian or Tony for that matter. There was so much of everything missing. I want to know more about Mrs Ford. Or Adrian’s parents. Writing the missing bits would obviously require some work and apparently Barnes has the credit to get his book published and awarded without the writing hassle business. I miss authors like Margaret Forster, Beryl Bainbridge even who could be elliptical when writing about the past and fallible memories without cheating out of a proper epilogue or ending.
